class.name: Joint3D
class.brief_description: Abstract base class for all 3D physics joints.
class.description: Abstract base class for all joints in 3D physics. 3D joints bind together two physics bodies ([member node_a] and [member node_b]) and apply a constraint. If only one body is defined, it is attached to a fixed [StaticBody3D] without collision shapes.

method.name: get_reaction_force
method.description: Returns the force (in newtons) the joint exerted on the second body during the last physics step in which it was solved, in world space. If the second body is static or kinematic, the negated force on the first body is returned instead. Returns a zero vector for joints that are sleeping or not simulated by Godot Physics. [b]Note:[/b] Only implemented by Godot Physics. Jolt Physics always returns a zero vector.

method.name: get_reaction_torque
method.description: Returns the torque (in newton-meters) the joint applied to the second body about its center of mass during the last solved physics step. This includes the moment of the reaction force when the joint is anchored away from the center of mass. Same fallback and backend limitations as [method get_reaction_force].

method.name: get_rid
method.description: Returns the joint's internal [RID] from the [PhysicsServer3D].

method.name: is_broken
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the joint was torn apart because its reaction exceeded [member break_force] or [member break_torque]. Changing the connected nodes reconfigures the joint and clears this state.

members.member: The force (in newtons) above which the joint breaks and releases both bodies. [code]0[/code] makes the joint unbreakable. Emits [signal broken]. [b]Note:[/b] Only supported by Godot Physics.
The torque (in newton-meters) above which the joint breaks and releases both bodies. [code]0[/code] makes the joint unbreakable. Emits [signal broken]. [b]Note:[/b] Only supported by Godot Physics.
If [code]true[/code], the two bodies bound together do not collide with each other.

Path to the first node (A) attached to the joint. The node must inherit [PhysicsBody3D]. If left empty and [member node_b] is set, the body is attached to a fixed [StaticBody3D] without collision shapes.

Path to the second node (B) attached to the joint. The node must inherit [PhysicsBody3D]. If left empty and [member node_a] is set, the body is attached to a fixed [StaticBody3D] without collision shapes.

The priority specifies how accurately a joint is solved. Generally, higher values improve accuracy. This has very different implementations between Godot Physics and Jolt Physics: [b]Godot Physics:[/b] [i]Values above 1 have a performance impact[/i]. Joint is solved [code]max(1, solver_priority) * iterations[/code] times. A value of [code]4[/code] would solve the same joint [i]4× additional times per physics step[/i]. [b]Jolt Physics:[/b] Aside from sorting the joints, there is no performance impact with higher values. Joints with [i]high[/i] priorities are solved [i]later[/i]. A value of [code]4[/code] would solve [i]after priorities of 0, 1, 2, and 3[/i]. Later joints have the final say between the two bodies they connect. Negative values are not allowed and will be silently [code]max(0, solver_priority)[/code] when set.

signal.name: broken
signal.description: Emitted after the joint broke because it exceeded [member break_force] or [member break_torque]. It is emitted on the main thread, deferred from the physics step.
